question: Ticket a577fd03e307 says 'outline 6.6.3.7 claims the hostname only (bounds/out explicitly excludes OS-family checks as out of scope)', but outline 6.6.3.7 reads "The hostname comes from the system device. It answers which box (the short hostname, lowercased) and which OS family, and nothing else in Cairn asks the OS for the hostname. Callers reach it through the client tool it publishes (2.3.7.1.5), so a box names itself on every OS, Windows included, with no bus running. - akiendelllinux_cc_0" (Outline 6.6.3.7 states the system device 'answers which box (the short hostname, lowercased) and which OS family.' If the ticket's work is built as written—centralizing hostname calls while leaving 54 OS-family checks scattered across 25 files—then the system device would not be answering both sources of OS information as the outline requires. The system device cannot be the centralized point for 'which box and which OS family' if OS-family information still flows from 54 other sites. Additionally, outline 2.3.7.1.5 says the system device 'publishes the host's name and OS family' (singular publishes), indicating a single point of control for both.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
answer: Both stand; they do not conflict. Outline 6.6.3.7 has one exclusive clause, 'nothing else in Cairn asks the OS for the hostname', and that is exactly the call sites this ticket repoints. For OS family the outline says the system device answers it (6.6.3.7) and publishes it (2.3.7.1.5); it does: os_id() is in cairn.devices.system_rackmount.tools.host.host, built by 5ccc7f05c932. Neither line says no other code may test the OS family, so the 54 OS-family checks are outside both the outline's exclusivity and this ticket's claim, and repointing them would be a new intention, not this one's missing half. Read from the whys already in the outline, so CC's (outline 0.4.1).
